articles.title: DNA Reveals Britain's 'Oldest Northerner' Was a 3-Year-Old Girl Buried 11,000 Years Ago
articles.summary: The oldest human remains in northern Britain belong to a girl aged 2.5–3.5 years, DNA shows. Found in a Cumbrian cave, the burial included jewelry from the same period, suggesting ritual significance. She is the third oldest known Mesolithic burial in northwestern Europe.

articles.title: Cosmic Rendezvous: Crescent Moon and Venus Dazzle in Global Photo Op
articles.summary: A razor-thin crescent moon and Venus made a spectacular close approach on May 18–19, visible worldwide. Earthshine illuminated the moon's dark limb, while Venus shone brilliantly. Photographers captured the pair above landmarks from New York to Sweden, with Jupiter joining the scene in Italy.

articles.title: DNA from Poop Helps Scientists Find New Homes for the World's Rarest Marsupial
articles.summary: With fewer than 150 Gilbert's potoroos left, researchers used eDNA metabarcoding on scat to decode their fungal diet. The non-invasive method revealed dietary overlap with quokkas and quendas, guiding translocation site selection after a 2015 wildfire destroyed 90% of their core habitat.
